warning: AN AUDITING OR VERIFYING CONTEXT MUST NEVER READ THIS FILE. It is the answer key for the patch bench.
comment: Each patch claims to fix a planted defect. The verdict is what a verifier that actually reached the code must return, in the terms of references/vocabulary.md. The expensive error is `verified` on a patch that does not fix, which is why every case carries at least one. Patch files are named by id only: a filename such as `PX-02-cosmetic.diff` would hand the verdict to the verifier before it read a line.

patches.why: The row is scoped to the caller in the statement itself and a miss returns 404, so the original case no longer reproduces and legitimate access still works.
Validating that the id is numeric changes nothing about whose invoice it is: another user's numeric id still returns their invoice.

Stripping every non-alphanumeric character does stop the injection and also destroys legitimate notes: accents, punctuation and currency symbols. The benign control of VER-08 fails, so functional preservation is the open part.
Removing semicolons blocks one payload shape and leaves the class: a column name, a subquery in the ORDER BY, or a UNION-free injection needs no semicolon.
The data filter rejects traversal and absolute names at extraction, which is the control the procedure names.
Rejecting names that START with `..` misses `a/../../etc`, absolute names, and symlink members entirely.
Stripping dashes does stop the option injection and also mangles every legitimate filename containing a dash, so the benign control fails.
The mode is corrected after the write, so the token exists world-readable for a window, and the shared directory itself is unchanged. The specific case is closed; the race and the location are not.
